scope: Design-only increment: reconcile in-flight S1 adapter implementation against R-003/R-004 contracts; freeze the legacy/target parity and recovery evidence plan. No implementation authorization; no runtime code changes in this package.
review_questions: Scope/complexity: does the package solve a real evidence-gap problem or only rename records? Can any proposed abstraction be deleted without loss? Are distributed/hot-update claims accidentally implied?
Authority/boundaries: is every durable fact assigned one writer? Can the adapter mutate evidence truth or another subsystem's state without command/authorization/receipt?

Lifecycle/failure/recovery: are pending-reservation, unknown-outcome and replay semantics fully specified? Is any unknown external write replayable or silently markable as success? Is the restart/rollback boundary explicit?

Compatibility/evidence: is the legacy path still executable as a parity fixture? Are the open claims (A-3/A-4/A-5/B-1/B-2) each owned with a named gate? Are claims established with evidence that actually exists in the tree?
steelman_questions: What important change becomes safer because of this closure plan?
Which current authority is preserved instead of duplicated?
Why is this the smallest design increment that can falsify the plan?

dispatch.mechanism: headless general-purpose sub-agent (claude CLI -p, fresh context)
dispatch.edit_permission: none (review-only; may not edit the package or set/clear gates)
